# LITs with `tags` `mathematical-statistics`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Mathematical statistics** — the theory of statistical inference read for itself — comparison and sufficiency of experiments (Blackwell, Le Cam deficiency), statistical decision theory, the sufficiency theorems (Fisher–Neyman, Basu, Bahadur) and bounds on estimation. Bayesian modelling is probabilistic-modeling (ADR-031).

| [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md) | A synthetic approach to Markov kernels, conditional independence and theorems on sufficient statistics | Fritz (2020), Adv. Math. 370:107239. Markov categories as a framework for synthetic probability and statistics: conditioning, conditional independence, almost-sure equality and sufficient statistics stated in categorical terms, with the Fisher–Neyman, Basu and Bahadur theorems proved there. Basu needs no extra axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur need strict positivity, not conditionals. Fisher–Neyman is matched to the classical theorem only in FinStoch. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md)); worth reading as the reference account of Markov categories and of how much probability and statistics follows from copying, discarding and composing kernels: determinism, four notions of conditional independence with the semigraphoid rules (weak union only with conditionals), almost-sure equality, and sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity. Basu's theorem holds in every Markov category, and Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur under strict positivity, which Stoch has without conditionals. The abstract Fisher–Neyman is matched to the classical theorem only for finite sets. |

| [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md) | Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments | Blackwell (1953), Ann. Math. Statist. 24(2):265–272. Completes the Blackwell order: for finitely many states, one experiment is at least as informative as another for every decision problem exactly when the other is a garbling of it. The easy direction is Blackwell (1951) and the finite converse Sherman and Stein's; this paper re-proves the converse by minimax, extends it to arbitrary outcome spaces by a martingale argument, introduces comparison by k-action problems, and reduces two-state comparison to the type I/type II error trade-off. | Active — read 2026-10-09 ([NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md)); worth reading as the paper in which the comparison of experiments is settled in general: for experiments with finitely many states, being at least as informative in every decision problem (Bohnenblust, Shapley and Sherman's order) and being able to reproduce the other by a stochastic transformation (Blackwell's 1951 sufficiency, later called garbling) are the same order. The finite-outcome converse is Sherman and Stein's, re-proved here by a minimax argument; the extension to arbitrary outcome spaces, by martingale convergence, is new. It adds comparison by k-action problems, and shows that for two states testing problems, and so the type I/type II error curves, decide the order. |

| [LIT-964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-964.md) v2 | The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis | Dwork et al. (2015). Adaptive reuse of data inflates false discoveries. By the Supplementary Material: if the max-information between the data and the function an analyst picks is at most log₂e·τ²n, that function's empirical mean exceeds its true mean by τ with probability at most e^{−τ²n}, and ε-differential privacy bounds max-information by log₂e·εn. Thresholdout answers m adaptively chosen [0, 1]-valued queries on a holdout to accuracy τ with probability 1 − β for n = O(ln(m/β)/τ²·min{B, √(B ln(m/β))/τ}), B the budget of detected overfits. The main text was not read. | Active — read 2026-10-14 ([NOTE-848](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-848.md)) in part; worth reading for [QUESTION-040](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-040.md) as a high-probability bound on overfitting under adaptive reuse: bounded max-information between the data and the analyst's choices bounds the chance a chosen statistic overfits, differential privacy bounds max-information, and Thresholdout validates m adaptively chosen statistical queries with a holdout growing as ln m. Read it knowing that only the Supplementary Material was reached, not the main text, that four of its six bounds are proved in companion papers, and that it covers [0, 1]-valued queries on a discrete universe. |

| [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md) | Stability of nonlinear Hawkes processes | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), Ann. Probab. 24(3): 1563–1588. Sufficient conditions for a Hawkes process with a nonlinear rate function and kernels of either sign to have a unique stationary version that versions started from a suitable past converge to: Lipschitz constant times the kernel's absolute mass below one (for networks, a spectral radius below one), or a bounded Lipschitz rate with no limit on kernel size.
